name: Blake Bauman
title: Principal Technical Architect

hero.headline: Enterprise-scale systems, edge computing, and AI.

summary: I'm a Principal Technical Architect at Adobe. For Fortune 500 clients I architect and ship enterprise commerce on Adobe Commerce and AEM Edge Delivery Services — including one of the first production EDS plus Commerce B2B integrations — and increasingly the agentic layer on top of it via Adobe Agent Orchestrator. I know how Commerce systems fail, how to migrate them, and how to build teams around them.

Outside client work I build agent infrastructure across three layers: the harness (Felix, a managed-agents harness on Cloudflare Workers with manifest-defined agents, swappable session strategies, and an agentic commerce layer), the evaluation layer (Memoturn, an open-source AI engineering platform for building, evaluating, and monitoring LLM applications in production — tracing, evals, prompt registry, cost analytics), and the governance layer (Fold, an enterprise MCP gateway in Go that federates every MCP server behind one governed endpoint with deny-by-default policy and credential brokering). Earlier iterations of this work ran on AWS Bedrock, AgentCore, and LangGraph. The list below is the live record; the chatbot below it answers questions about it.

projects.name: felix
projects.description: Managed agents harness on Cloudflare Workers, shaped after Anthropic's Managed Agents architecture. Manifest-defined agents compile into runnable agents exposed over OpenAI-compatible chat, A2A, MCP, and REST/SSE — with Felix Commerce, an agentic commerce layer (Agentic Commerce Protocol merchant endpoint, approval-gated Stripe checkout, per-brand D2C storefronts, B2B quote-to-cash), on top.
projects.context: Three swappable seams: session strategies (full replay, windowed, summarizing, semantic), pattern and model-provider registries (ReAct, Deep, Router, Parallel, GroupChat, Reflect, Plan-Execute across Anthropic, OpenAI, and Workers AI), and transport-labelled tool executors (local, MCP, A2A, container, sandbox, browser, queue). Includes HITL approvals, append-only audit log, eval harness with golden datasets, guardrails, and A2A federation. Evolved from an earlier AWS Bedrock + LangGraph implementation. Docs at docs.felix.run.

projects.name: fold
projects.description: Enterprise MCP gateway — one governed endpoint between every MCP client and every MCP server. Federates multiple servers behind namespaced tools with deny-by-default ABAC policy, JWT/JWKS auth with OAuth token exchange (RFC 8693), and credential brokering so agents never hold raw API keys.
projects.context: Single static Go binary (~22 MB distroless image) on the official MCP Go SDK, with optional Redis for distributed fleet state. Rate limiting, circuit breakers, caching, load balancing with health checks, dynamic registry discovery, hot config reload, a console UI, and a Kubernetes discovery controller with Helm chart. Structured audit events for every request (including denials) plus OpenTelemetry tracing and Prometheus metrics. Passes the official MCP conformance suite 40/40; v1.4.1 with the API contract frozen at v1.0.0, hardened with fuzzers and chaos tests.

projects.name: memoturn
projects.description: Open-source AI engineering platform for building, evaluating, and monitoring LLM applications in production — tracing and observability over OpenTelemetry, an evaluation framework spanning offline datasets, online production sampling, and human review, a versioned prompt registry with deployment channels, and cost/token/latency dashboards.
projects.context: Hono API on Bun with a Vite + TanStack Router SPA; PostgreSQL via Prisma for OLTP and Apache Doris for OLAP analytics, with Redis/Valkey and BullMQ for background work and S3-compatible storage for artifacts. Ships TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs with LangChain and OpenAI integrations, a multi-provider playground with streaming, SSO/RBAC/audit logs, and an MCP server that exposes prompts and datasets to agent IDEs.

recognition.title: 2nd Place: Adobe AI Summit & Hackathon
recognition.description: We built a content generation plugin for Adobe DA.live that uses Adobe Commerce catalog data, multi-agent workflow using Langchain domain agents, and LLMs to generate AEM-ready product content. Features context-aware generation, real-time WebSocket streaming, batch page updates, and Adobe Firefly integration.

experience.description: Delivered one of the first production AEM Edge Delivery Services plus Adobe Commerce B2B integrations, for a Fortune 500 company. Ran a webinar on Commerce with Edge Delivery that became a reference for Adobe's enterprise teams.
Led migration of a global beverage company from Adobe Commerce on-prem to Cloud, with zero downtime. Built the architectural review process for enterprise Commerce implementations.

Led design and implementation of Adobe Commerce for a leading activewear company. Spearheaded Adobe Scene7 integration to optimize product imagery, improving visual merchandising and site performance.
